finding.claim: Unauthenticated /fetch handler passes the `target` query parameter straight to http.Get, so any caller can make the server request arbitrary URLs, including loopback, private-range and cloud metadata addresses (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/). The response body is streamed back to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the body copied to the response via io.Copy at main.go:22

trace.note: http.HandleFunc("/fetch", fetch) registers the route with no auth middleware
target is read from the query string without any validation
http.Get(target) issues the outbound request; the default client follows redirects and has no timeout
the upstream response body is returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, or private/loopback/link-local IP blocking. No authentication on the route. The `allowed` map is used only by safeFetch, not by fetch. The default http.Client is used and follows redirects.

verdict.reason: main.go:15 reads `target` from the query string and main.go:16 passes it unvalidated to http.Get, with the body returned at main.go:22 and the route registered with no auth at main.go:41; the `allowed` check exists only in safeFetch (main.go:27).
